The Government of Sikkim’s Finance Department officially issued Notification No. 03/FIN/ADM through Extraordinary Gazette No. 303. Enacted under clause (3) of Article 166 of the Constitution of India, the Sikkim Government Vehicle Procurement and Maintenance Rules, 2025 establish clear procedures, financial ceilings, entitlements, and operational guidelines governing all official state vehicles.

1. Key Definitions & Operational Framework

The rules apply to all government vehicles—including two-wheelers, passenger cars, utility pick-ups, and heavy vehicles—across state departments.

item.title: Standardizing Transparency: A Complete Guide to Proactive Disclosure Under Section 4 of the RTI Act
item.description:
Transparency in public administration forms the cornerstone of accountability and public trust. Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, mandates every public authority to proactively disclose detailed organizational data. This statutory requirement ensures that citizens have seamless access to routine administrative records without having to repeatedly file individual RTI requests.

To streamline compliance across municipal, state, and central institutions, adopting a structured, standardized, and fillable template is essential. Below is a comprehensive, end-to-end framework that public authorities can implement to fulfill all statutory requirements under Section 4(1)(b).

item.title: Strengthening Public Financial Management: A Comprehensive Guide to Internal Audit Guidelines and the 3 E's
item.description:
Introduction

In the realm of public governance, ensuring financial accountability, transparency, and optimal utilization of public resources is paramount. Governments handle vast amounts of public funds, execute complex programs, and manage extensive assets. To maintain fiscal discipline and prevent irregularities, organizations rely heavily on robust oversight mechanisms. Among these, the Internal Audit Organisation acts as a crucial catalyst from within, safeguarding public funds and streamlining department functions.

This blog explores the comprehensive framework governing internal audits—drawing from foundational guidelines (such as the 1992 and 2005 supplementary regulations)—while diving deep into core concepts like internal control mechanisms and the classic performance framework known as the 3 E’s (Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness).

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Local Body Audits: Comprehensive Requisition Checklists, Financial Formats, and Compliance Frameworks for GPUs, ZPs, and Municipalities
item.description:
Conducting a statutory or internal audit of local self-government institutions—such as Gram Panchayat Units (GPUs), Zilla Panchayats (ZPs), and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) or Municipalities—requires a structured, systematic approach. Auditing these bodies involves verifying not only cash transactions and bank balances but also statutory compliance, public procurement guidelines, revenue realisations, and asset registers.

This comprehensive guide compiles every essential checklist, fillable requisition format, financial reporting template, and technical explanation needed to prepare for or execute an audit of local governing bodies.

item.title: Building an Automated eGramSwaraj Data Extractor: Streamlining Municipal Audit Workflows
item.description:
Building an Automated eGramSwaraj Data Extractor: Streamlining Municipal Audit Workflows

Introduction

Conducting financial audits across local governance bodies—such as Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies—often presents a classic data management bottleneck: portals like eGramSwaraj house thousands of crucial expenditure vouchers, payment records, and development scheme allocations, but extracting this data into structured formats for audit sampling can be tedious and prone to manual error.

To solve this, we developed a lightweight, client-side JavaScript extraction script that hooks directly into the browser DOM while inspecting eGramSwaraj data views. This tool automates the aggregation of voucher numbers, dates, beneficiary details, payment amounts, and scheme heads, exporting everything into clean, standardized CSV files ready for audit analysis.
